Challenging judgment and award dated 01.12.2014 passed by Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranebennur in MVC No.393/2012, this appeal is filed by appellant-insurer.

2 2.

Brief facts as stated are that on 08.10.2011 when Shekappa S/o Nagappa Jadar was proceeding on his bicycle from Hosur to Hirekerur, rider of motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-27/U-1922,
riding it in rash and negligent manner dashed against bicycle of Shekappa causing accident.

In accident, said Shekappa sustained grievous injuries and was shifted to Government Hospital,
Hirekerur and thereafter, shifted to CJ, Hospital Davanagere.
Despite being treated further at Bapuji Hospital, Davanagere and Manipal Hospital, he did not survive.
3. Claiming compensation on account of untimely death, his wife and children filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
4. Claim petition was contested by owner and insurer denying rash and negligence on behalf of rider of motorcycle and alleging negligence against deceased.
It was also alleged by insurer that deceased had consumed alcohol and was therefore, negligent in causing accident.
5. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and additional issues and thereafter, recorded evidence of claimant no.1 as PW1 and marked Exhibits P1 to P14.
On behalf of respondents, five witnesses as RW1 to RW6 were examined and Exhibits R1 to R13 were marked.

6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and as it was insured with insurer, claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.6,88,400/- with 6% interest per annum from insurer.
7. Aggrieved by said award, insurer is in appeal.
8. Shri M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel appearing for appellant-insurer submitted that, tribunal was not justified in fastening entire negligence against rider of motorcycle.
It was submitted that deceased was riding bicycle under influence of alcohol and therefore, contributed to accident.
9. On other hand, learned counsel for respondents sought to support award and opposed appeal.

10. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award and record.
11.
From above submission, occurrence of accident and death of Shekappa in said accident is not in dispute.
Involvement of insured vehicle and validity of insurance policy as on date of accident is also not in dispute.
Insurer is in appeal challenging finding on negligence.

Therefore, only point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether assessment of negligence entirely against rider of motorcycle by tribunal was justified?"
12.

On perusal of impugned award it is seen that, tribunal arrived at its conclusion by referring to police investigation records wherein, complaint registered against rider of motorcycle and after investigation, charge-sheet is filed only against rider of motorcycle.

As against said evidence,
absolutely no material is placed on record by insurer insofar as negligence.

The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Ratnamma on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179965688/
3 13.
Under circumstances, I do not find any justification to interfere with finding of tribunal.
14. Insofar as quantum of compensation, though it may require some re-computation but on over all consideration, compensation awarded appears to be just and proper.
Therefore, there is no interference.
Point for consideration is answered in affirmative.

15. Consequently following:
ORDER Appeal is devoid of merit and is dismissed.
Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal for payment.
Insurer is directed to deposit balance compensation within a period of six weeks.
